correctness.rationale: O'Hara supplies uniqueness for the relevant convex planar \(r^{-2}\)-center. Reflection therefore places the center on the symmetry altitude. Finch records Shibata's equal angle-to-area ratios. The base subtriangle has area fraction \(q\), so its central angle is \(2\pi q\), while direct isosceles geometry gives \(2\arctan(1/(\lambda q))\); equating them yields \(\lambda q\tan(\pi q)=1\). The left side is strictly increasing from 0 to infinity on \(q\in(0,1/2)\), proving exact uniqueness. Implicit differentiation proves strict decrease in \(\lambda\), and standard tangent/cotangent expansions prove both asymptotics. The bundled checker reproduces Finch's decimal and sampled identities but is only diagnostic.

value.rationale: The isosceles family is a canonical one-parameter shape class, and the theorem converts a published numerical center computation into an exact scale-free equation valid for every member, with strict aspect-ratio monotonicity and two degeneration asymptotics. This is a natural structural reduction of a named geometric center, not an arbitrary numerical slice or a recomputation of a known table value.
